guides.title: Do twelve-part diagrams behave like named cycles?
guides.tested: Compared the order of written tokens around a twelve-part diagram with historical naming traditions, allowing rotations and reversals.
guides.found: The exact-order matches did not stand out from shuffled sector orders. Historical name forms were collected, but no diagram was identified as a sequence of signs, houses, or months.
guides.unresolved: The reading order and the connection between a sector and a particular name remain unestablished. No sound values were fitted.

guides.title: Comparing descriptions and instructions
guides.tested: Compared repetition and word-part patterns in Chaucer's astrolabe text with selected Voynich passages.
guides.found: Chaucer repeated whole words more often, while Voynich endings were more concentrated. These are descriptive differences between the selected samples.
guides.unresolved: Spelling systems, alphabets, edited text, and mixed passage types make direct interpretation difficult. This did not validate a way to identify instructions or translate them.

guides.title: Which zodiac labels are actually comparable?
guides.tested: Inspected paired Aries and Taurus images and compared the written forms associated with their labels and rings.
guides.found: Some unusual spelling candidates survived comparison across readings, but no isolated Voynich word was established as the sign's name. The later readable month annotations were kept separate.
guides.unresolved: A label near an animal can refer to something else. Image placement and spelling ranks do not establish a name, a pronunciation, or a decipherment.

guides.title: Are there enough securely identified zodiac names?
guides.tested: Inventoried surviving zodiac panels, their labels, alternate readings, and historical written sign names.
guides.found: Twelve panels supplied ten sign identities, but not ten securely identified Voynich name tokens. Transcription gaps and a disagreement over scribal attribution were retained.
guides.unresolved: The link from pictured sign to written word is missing. A name-decoding benchmark with supplied name pairs cannot be transferred to these uncertain labels.

guides.title: Did saved attachments contain genuinely untouched passages?
guides.tested: Audited saved research attachments and their exposure history for a protected word-sequence test reserve.
guides.found: No genuine protected passage reserve was established. Some references to held-out material concerned image judgments or a model's training split, rather than text nobody had previously inspected.
guides.unresolved: An untouched annotation can still concern already exposed text. The audit did not authorize new scoring or manufacture a fresh reserve.

guides.title: Can the proposed B/C scoring adapters recover known answers?
guides.tested: Tested the adapters on constructed examples with known numerical and phrase-order relationships, including several arrangements of item counts.
guides.found: Most arrangements worked, but three groups of four items failed positive recovery. An exact counting argument showed that this arrangement could not meet the frozen significance threshold, even with a perfect match.
guides.unresolved: The adapters did not qualify across every required condition. Success on other arrangements does not authorize use on real B/C data.

guides.title: Repairing a test for differences between contexts
guides.tested: Repaired a statistical baseline and checked it on constructed examples before applying the qualified version to the retrospective manuscript comparison.
guides.found: The repaired version passed its declared calibration checks. The manuscript comparison detected no within-scribe differences in effect strength.
guides.unresolved: The test had limited ability to detect moderate differences. No detection does not establish that the effect is constant, and the text was already exposed or uncertified as untouched.

guides.title: A replacement test that failed calibration
guides.tested: Tested a proposed replacement for comparing effect strength between contexts, using cases where the true answer was known.
guides.found: The replacement flagged differences too often in a required control with differing baseline rates. It failed the frozen calibration requirement, so the manuscript comparison was not run.
guides.unresolved: Passing a separate practical-tolerance check did not cancel that failure. The historical question remained unanswered by this version.

guides.title: How large a difference could the repaired test detect?
guides.tested: Used constructed effects on the manuscript's actual support pattern to measure the unchanged repaired test's sensitivity.
guides.found: Reliable detection generally required large differences, with thresholds depending on context and transcription. Every tested twelve-percentage-point difference fell below the required sensitivity target.
guides.unresolved: These are conditional simulation results, not estimates of the manuscript's true differences or a universal detection limit. Some cases remained inconclusive or impossible to construct.

guides.title: Rebuilding a proposed substitution-decoding method
guides.tested: Implemented an adaptation of a published alphagram and language-model search, testing multiple reading directions and traversal choices.
guides.found: The automatic coherence selection failed: all 200 selected primary items consisted only of unknown-word placeholders. The scoring system rewarded missing vocabulary rather than useful readable output.
guides.unresolved: The unavailable original executable, unspecified source details, and recorded adaptations prevent an exact-replication claim. No selected output was established as a translation.

guides.title: Diagnosing the unknown-word scoring failure
guides.tested: Separated and repaired several ways the earlier language model handled unknown words, sentence endings, and missing contexts, then tested the repair on known-answer controls.
guides.found: The repair still failed required qualification checks in both source arms. Some individual tests improved, but neither arm qualified as a whole.
guides.unresolved: Correcting a ranking formula alone could not repair keys already fitted with a defective objective. New manuscript scoring stayed closed.

guides.title: Separating scorer, decoder, objective, and search failures
guides.tested: Made a narrower sentence-ending repair and tested probability arithmetic, discrimination, true-key decoding, the search objective, and blind key search separately.
guides.found: Probability arithmetic was repaired, but the full system remained unqualified. The separate checks exposed limits beyond that arithmetic bug, including weak discrimination and search performance.
guides.unresolved: A mathematically valid scorer is not automatically an effective decoder. Fresh evidence from additional human writers was unavailable, and old material could not be made fresh by resampling.

guides.title: Do proposed category assignments travel to other passages?
guides.tested: Kept the worksheet's proposed word categories fixed and examined their neighbors and positions on additional folios.
guides.found: The extension preserved alternate readings, unassigned words, and counterexamples instead of inventing categories for every new neighbor. The counts did not qualify a semantic model.
guides.unresolved: The additional text came from an already inventoried corpus. Consistent-looking category substitutions still need independent evidence about what the words refer to.

guides.title: Trying competing interpretations without calling them translations
guides.tested: Built an exploratory worksheet for substituting proposed categories into selected passages and comparing competing interpretations.
guides.found: Several broad assignments can be made structurally compatible with selected text. None earned a demonstrated semantic advantage, and unassigned words and uncertainties stayed visible.
guides.unresolved: A plausible category pattern does not identify an ingredient, planet, procedure, or preparation. Useful progress would require consistent predictions and independently supported referents.

guides.title: Are recurring word combinations more than frequency effects?
guides.tested: Compared recurring pairs and triples with shuffled versions of the same lines, preserving word counts, boundaries, and important layout conditions.
guides.found: None of the 276 paired patterns passed the corrected test in both main readings. The stricter correction and the earlier result were both retained.
guides.unresolved: The test was conservative and weak for rare combinations. This does not show that the manuscript lacks phrases or ordinary language, and it supplies no meanings.

guides.title: A complete inventory of written forms
guides.tested: Built a searchable inventory of characters, proposed sign groups, word parts, sequences, and complete words across the available transcriptions.
guides.found: The atlas exposes rare forms as well as frequent ones, with filters for section, hand, layout, page, and position. Unknown slots and incomplete spatial mapping remain explicit.
guides.unresolved: Alternate transcriptions describe the same manuscript rather than independent texts. Written units in this atlas are not established syllables, grammatical categories, or meanings.

guides.title: Testing links between text, pictures, and recurring frames
guides.tested: Organized separate studies of image/text relationships and recurring text frames, with rules intended to prevent discovery choices from leaking into confirmation.
guides.found: The initial report records several blocked or incomplete arms. Later source-control work includes a narrowly qualified replacement control bank, but the class-based manuscript discovery found no eligible candidate to confirm.
guides.unresolved: This folder has a long sequence of amendments and follow-ups; its initial report is not a complete current summary. Independent image judgments, source support, and unopened confirmation remain distinct requirements.

guides.title: Why did the spelling-class frame search find nothing?
guides.tested: Audited each frozen discovery requirement against every screened early paragraph frame.
guides.found: Every manuscript frame missed the required paragraph-presence threshold; recurrence rejected nearly all of them as well. The selected Latin positive frames met the requirements.
guides.unresolved: The audit preserved the no-candidate result and did not lower thresholds or open confirmation. The Latin transformations were one source, not independent positive corpora.

guides.title: Applying the qualified spelling-class frame search
guides.tested: Used the fixed spelling-class engine on discovery paragraphs separately for two scribes.
guides.found: Neither discovery panel supplied an eligible frame. Both null selections were frozen, and all four confirmation cells remained untested.
guides.unresolved: No candidate means there was nothing eligible to transfer under these rules. It is not a general rejection of formulas, grammar, or every possible encoding.

guides.title: The first spelling-class control bank
guides.tested: Replaced exact-word identities with one fixed set of fifty-two operational spelling classes and tested the full discovery/confirmation pipeline.
guides.found: The reused Latin positives passed, but ten invalid generations among the scheduled control trials blocked qualification under the frozen rule. The valid negatives were not pooled with invalid trials to claim success.
guides.unresolved: Spelling classes are not linguistic morphology. The failed bank remains failed despite the later separate replacement.

guides.title: A fresh isolated replacement control bank
guides.tested: Retested the unchanged class-based method on a separately registered bank with isolated workers.
guides.found: All 1,200 trials were valid and none produced a full passing control result; the reused Latin positive cells also passed. The method received limited control qualification on this bank.
guides.unresolved: The earlier failed bank is preserved separately. One exposed Latin source and fixed constructed mechanisms do not establish broad positive power on manuscript-scale material.

guides.title: Saved generator outputs for the T3 controls
guides.tested: Stored the generated material used by the parent T3 qualification studies.
guides.found: This is a supporting-output container rather than a separate study or a new set of independent findings. Its interpretation comes from the parent protocols and control reports.
guides.unresolved: File counts are not independent sample sizes. Do not infer an overall qualification from the presence of successfully generated files.

guides.title: Explaining the exact-word frame search's negative discovery
guides.tested: Checked which frozen criteria eliminated the complete universe of screened early frames.
guides.found: Every manuscript frame failed both the required paragraph presence and the repeated-variant criterion. The known Latin positives behaved differently under these same rules.
guides.unresolved: The diagnosis did not retune the method or promote near misses. It explains this registered result rather than ruling out all formula-like text.

guides.title: Searching for exact anchors with a variable multiword gap
guides.tested: Applied the qualified exact-word frame engine to discovery paragraphs with separate scribe panels.
guides.found: Both panels returned no candidate, so the registered terminal rule left confirmation closed. No confirmation p-values were calculated.
guides.unresolved: This is a result about the fixed frame definition and thresholds. It supplies no semantic interpretation or general absence claim.

guides.title: Qualifying the multiword revision on controls
guides.tested: Allowed a one-to-three-word variable slot between exact anchor words, with fixed discovery and transfer requirements.
guides.found: The reused Latin degree-slot positive was recovered through all four fixed transformations, and none of the 1,200 fresh native-mechanism datasets supplied a discovery candidate. This met limited control qualification.
guides.unresolved: The four positives transform one exposed source block. The earlier single-word failure remains preserved, and manuscript confirmation was not part of this control-only run.

guides.title: Testing a positional-slot alternative
guides.tested: Prepared a separately frozen positional-slot engine, engineering oracles, Latin checks, and native control generation.
guides.found: The saved Latin qualification is failed: each of its four cells failed the required predictions. Generation ledgers and engineering successes do not replace that positive-control requirement.
guides.unresolved: The snapshot does not supply a successful overall qualification or opened manuscript confirmation. Read the separate gate receipts rather than treating the file inventory as completion.

guides.title: Does the original frame rule work on a known historical source?
guides.tested: Acquired and checked a printed Latin materia-medica block, then ran the original rule through the fixed transformations.
guides.found: All four positive discovery cells returned no candidate. The method therefore remained unqualified, despite the source's explicit early quality statements.
guides.unresolved: The witness is a later print of a medieval work, not a diplomatic manuscript transcription. Failed controls and source corrections were retained, and confirmation stayed closed.

guides.title: Why did contextual-role recovery fail?
guides.tested: Examined the saved errors and score components from the preceding role-recovery experiment without fitting a new model.
guides.found: Exact context features were sparse, clusters often followed local boundaries or collocations, and unseen features introduced a concrete scoring bias. The audit did not show that the representation had exhausted all useful information.
guides.unresolved: Wider context was a possible future experiment, not an established cure. Retrospective error explanations are not prospective recovery improvements.

guides.title: Does backing off from rare word pairs help?
guides.tested: Suppressed singleton context-pair evidence while retaining the component words already present in the repaired scorer.
guides.found: The fixed rule changed very few decisions, produced negligible recovery improvement, and added no coverage. Simply falling back from an unseen pair was already equivalent to the baseline unless evidence was counted twice.
guides.unresolved: This particular rule was not adopted. Other ways of sharing or combining evidence were not established by this test.

guides.title: Sharing word identity across nearby positions
guides.tested: Added shared word-identity evidence while retaining position-specific context, with a duplication control for comparison.
guides.found: The candidate made more decisions and improved observed role recovery on the supported development panels. Its probability estimates worsened, including greater confidence in some wrong answers, and the corrected comparisons did not confirm the gain independently.
guides.unresolved: The candidate remained exploratory. Higher coverage and raw accuracy do not by themselves establish reliable confidence or generalization to new sources.

guides.title: Can local context recover independently labelled roles?
guides.tested: Tested automatic selection of the number of roles on constructed cases, then separately tested a fixed two-role method against external Latin annotations.
guides.found: Automatic role-count selection failed several required controls. The historical transfer produced no fully passing panel; some panels failed and others lacked enough support.
guides.unresolved: The failures apply to this representation, method, and sample. No Voynich roles or meanings were fitted, and a supervised diagnostic was not treated as successful blind discovery.

guides.title: Using shared evidence only when local evidence is absent
guides.tested: Tested a fixed positional-first fallback intended to retain sharing's extra coverage while reducing its confidence problems.
guides.found: The fallback kept the extra decisions but lost most of the earlier recovery gain. Confidence quality improved relative to additive sharing, yet did not meet the requested no-worse comparison with the repaired baseline.
guides.unresolved: This was a partial tradeoff rather than a complete solution. The exposed development results do not independently qualify the method.

guides.title: Does training frequency provide better evidence weights?
guides.tested: Weighted local and shared word evidence according to their training occurrence counts, alongside fixed comparison arms.
guides.found: This weighting rule did not improve expected recovery or probability-score quality over the repaired baseline. It retained extra coverage but lost to an equal-weight mixture on recovery in every adequately supported development panel.
guides.unresolved: Training counts are not automatically measures of reliability or independent evidence. No alternative weighting was selected after seeing the failure.

guides.title: Treating unseen context as missing evidence
guides.tested: Changed the supervised scorer so that globally unseen features contribute no evidence and completely unsupported cases remain undecided.
guides.found: The repair improved several development measures and the evidence-bearing subset, but also produced explicit abstentions. Counting abstentions as misses gives a different, less favorable result than assigning them half-credit.
guides.unresolved: No supported full comparison reached the recovery target. This repaired diagnostic did not qualify blind role discovery or establish any Voynich meanings.

guides.title: Completing image ratings and clarifying historical-key tests
guides.tested: Completed missing image-rating pairs, resolved the original short-line rule from its owning protocol, and prepared retrospective testing rules for published decipherment keys.
guides.found: The completed rating population passed its recorded agreement checks, and line-width classification was made explicit. Published-key scoring remained unrun because the required mappings and target resources were incomplete.
guides.unresolved: Agreement between raters does not prove what text means. A retrospective key test cannot be relabelled untouched confirmation, and the B/C bridge still required its own qualification.

guides.title: Seeing the actual words behind section differences
guides.tested: Collected the source lines and neighboring words behind the selected controlled word-part contrasts.
guides.found: The concordance makes recurring pairs, triples, alternate readings, and unknown slots inspectable. It describes where the selected patterns occur rather than running a new phrase-significance test.
guides.unresolved: Recurrence across pages is not automatically more than chance, and neither recurrence nor a section association supplies a meaning.

guides.title: Does the sh-to-qok association survive an availability restriction?
guides.tested: Asked whether a qok-starting next word was more frequent after sh than ch in the specified Currier A material, after removing structurally blocked followers.
guides.found: The separately qualified retrospective comparison passed in both main readings, with an effect of about four percentage points. This rules out the specified binary blocking explanation alone in these samples.
guides.unresolved: The text was already exposed or uncertified as untouched. Other spelling, junction, and register explanations remain possible; this is not a grammatical or semantic identification.

guides.title: How varied are the neighbors of daiin?
guides.tested: Compared neighboring-word diversity under matched sampling and tested a specific prediction about nearby content-word candidates.
guides.found: Neighbor diversity varied by section and hand, but none of the twelve content-prediction tests passed. Sparse comparison groups and hundreds of counterexamples were retained.
guides.unresolved: The results do not establish daiin as a function word, content word, rebus, or phonetic spelling. Descriptive ranks are not semantic evidence.

guides.title: Do daro-associated pages depict fennel?
guides.tested: Inspected the plant drawings on the selected daro-opening pages before consulting the detailed reference and competing identification notes.
guides.found: No convincing fennel candidate emerged from those pages. The most suggestive feathery silhouette resolved into broad toothed leaves on closer inspection.
guides.unresolved: The selection was exposed and not a blinded botanical identification. The result is limited to these drawings and does not reject a wider historical herb tradition.

guides.title: Which written forms distinguish manuscript sections?
guides.tested: Turned the earlier controlled word-part comparisons into a searchable ranking and inspection interface.
guides.found: The display retains the earlier twenty-one paired passing contrasts alongside direction disagreements, rare untested forms, and unsupported comparisons. It adds navigation rather than a new experiment.
guides.unresolved: A distinctive form is not a decoded meaning. Comparable spatial data were too sparse to treat inside/on/outside rankings as established location effects.

guides.title: Do repeated e signs vary differently in labels and prose?
guides.tested: Compared forms that differ only in their runs of e signs, requiring comparable examples on the same page and panel.
guides.found: The required Recipes comparison lacked enough examples in both formats. The supposed three-step illustrative family also needed correction: its longest form was not attested as a fully readable token.
guides.unresolved: Insufficient support is not evidence that the formats behave equally. A counting or numeral interpretation was not tested.

guides.title: When is it useful to pool word endings?
guides.tested: Tested a predictor on known text with planted redundant endings, informative endings, and layout-driven endings.
guides.found: The predictor separated the planted redundant and informative cases, but also accepted every layout-driven control. That prevents interpreting acceptance as proof of meaningless filler.
guides.unresolved: The exact natural-ending families and manuscript collapse were not qualified or run. Prediction improvement alone cannot decide what an ending does.

guides.title: Had supposedly fresh passages already entered earlier work?
guides.tested: Traced saved scripts, results, and conversations to distinguish simple availability from previous feature and neighbor analysis.
guides.found: The audit found substantial earlier exposure and did not establish a protected passage reserve. It carefully separated script selection scope from proof that a person inspected every token.
guides.unresolved: It did not prove that every remaining passage had already received the exact later direction test. It also did not create new untouched material or authorize scoring.

guides.title: Can prose opening signs explain a ring's boundary?
guides.tested: Compared prose f/p opening preferences with the actual image geometry of the disputed slot on the f57v diagram.
guides.found: The prose signs share an opening preference, but the ring slot is internal to its transcribed run and lacks the proposed immediate divider. Geometry from other rings could not supply its missing boundary.
guides.unresolved: The proposed direct boundary transfer was unsupported. Sparse exact matches also prevented a validated f-specific cross-format rule.

guides.title: A browser for manuscript word parts
guides.tested: Built filters and concordances for written characters, candidate sign groups, prefixes, suffixes, strings, and complete words.
guides.found: The atlas makes distributions inspectable by hand, section, format, and line position, while keeping the two main readings separate and treating unknown words as barriers.
guides.unresolved: This is an exploration tool, not automatic interpretation. Overlapping strings are not independent categories, and section differences do not identify meanings.

guides.title: Are rare g endings partly a reading or handwriting issue?
guides.tested: Inspected selected manuscript images and compared g/m classifications and positions across transcriptions.
guides.found: Graphic and encoding differences are plausible contributors to the apparent rarity. Some g-classified forms occur inside lines, so a strict line-ending-only account does not hold for all inspected examples.
guides.unresolved: The audit did not establish a universal g-to-m replacement or an expert decision that the forms are one sign. No names or sound values were refitted.

guides.title: Do opening-line sign preferences survive tighter matching?
guides.tested: Compared plume-class signs in otherwise identical word frames while matching page, position, writer, and additional layout conditions.
guides.found: The descriptive opening-line preference survived stricter matching, with p providing most of the support. Matching examples for f existed, but the reused test subset was too sparse for a firm f-specific rule.
guides.unresolved: This is retrospective consistency on exposed pages. It does not explain a ring's start, establish a mechanism, or provide untouched confirmation.

guides.title: Trying grouped signs as single alphabetic units
guides.tested: Treated selected EVA sign combinations as single units, qualified the restricted decoder on known text, then applied frozen Latin and German keys to reserved windows.
guides.found: The known-text checks succeeded, but the inspected manuscript outputs did not yield a coherent reading. Dictionary-word hits were recorded as vocabulary overlap rather than translation accuracy.
guides.unresolved: Only this group-to-letter scheme was tested. The result does not reject syllabic, rebus, or broader phonetic systems.

guides.title: Why were herbal relationships being missed?
guides.tested: Varied wording, reference handling, and passage boundaries in a frozen diagnosis of the herbal relation extractor.
guides.found: The variations changed the number of candidate links, but lacked independent correctness labels. Previously unprocessed source blocks supplied no recognized planets, leaving that fresh-block check inconclusive.
guides.unresolved: More extracted links are not automatically more accurate links. Medieval transfer and independently judged recipe relationships remained unqualified.

guides.title: Can a known herbal support reliable relationship extraction?
guides.tested: Tested rules connecting an herb entry to ingredients, planetary associations, preparation, and application while allowing abstention on uncertain references.
guides.found: The pilot recovered candidate relationships but failed one authored control and lacked independent historical labels. Its reused source reserve was not untouched confirmation.
guides.unresolved: Entry-level association cannot simply be inherited by every ingredient. No Voynich relationship scoring was opened.

guides.title: Finding possible ingredients, operations, and applications
guides.tested: Used known herbal text to look for explicit cues to several kinds of recipe information, keeping later and medieval material separate.
guides.found: The extractor found candidate coverage, but recipe boundaries and semantic correctness were not independently established. A heading-contamination bug and authored semantic failures were preserved.
guides.unresolved: The medieval sample was too small for transfer claims. The method did not qualify for manuscript scoring, and counts should not be read as accuracy.

guides.title: Preparing picture-only judgments
guides.tested: Built a source-only image-rating workflow intended to keep picture judgments separate from transcription and text analysis.
guides.found: The retained checkpoint is preparation rather than a completed image/text experiment: registration and ratings were pending, with substantial image-access failures and withheld ambiguous panels.
guides.unresolved: The older plant-match pilot was a different task. Its scorer and interface cannot stand in for reliable image-context annotation.

guides.title: Registering lines and independently marking pictures
guides.tested: Separated picture annotation from line geometry so that text/image relationships could eventually be tested without drawing the picture labels from the text.
guides.found: The archive preserves successive packet, registration, agreement, and completion stages. A later continuation completed missing rating pairs and passed its recorded full-population agreement checks.
guides.unresolved: The early README's zero-rating state is historical. Agreement between annotations does not itself establish the text/image hypothesis; use the dated completion and analysis receipts.

guides.title: A separate qok-rate-by-image study design
guides.tested: Specified a descriptive comparison of qok frequency across image categories while adjusting for section and keeping the earlier hypotheses unchanged.
guides.found: Arithmetic and token-counting checks passed on constructed examples. The retained design required source-owner timing evidence and qualified registration before any real image/text join.
guides.unresolved: A synthetic-only qualification is not a manuscript result. No semantic class, sound assignment, or claim-level significance follows from this design.

guides.title: Can written labels be linked reliably to depicted objects?
guides.tested: Developed a frozen label-to-object protocol, scientific controls, and independent image-registration pilots.
guides.found: The scientific qualification and registration gates did not pass. Neither two-pass registration pilot established usable accepted label geometry, and tiny vision-interface checks did not establish manuscript reliability.
guides.unresolved: No manuscript label/object claim test ran. Reliable independent registration, object ratings, and successful controls were still required; failed attempts and raw responses were preserved.

guides.title: A decoder that leaves unknown signs unknown
guides.tested: Qualified a restricted letter-mapping search on known text, then applied frozen Latin and German keys to separate manuscript windows.
guides.found: The controls showed that unresolved symbols could be masked correctly, but inspected manuscript output did not yield a coherent reading. Dictionary matches were not counted as translation accuracy.
guides.unresolved: This narrow search does not establish or reject phonetic or rebus writing. Unseen symbols, uncertain words, source contamination, and training restrictions remain important limits.

guides.title: Do three words behave alike outside one noticed frame?
guides.tested: Compared ol, qokedy, and qol after excluding the original page and every occurrence of the shared frame that motivated the question.
guides.found: The interface retains their other neighbors, directed pairs, common frames, and complete source passages, with separate denominators for each target.
guides.unresolved: These are descriptive comparisons of written words. Shared positions do not establish shared meanings, grammar, or an independently validated semantic class.

guides.title: How many supplied names does the toy decoder need?
guides.tested: Expanded the name-recovery benchmark with new name strings, separate development and confirmation sets, and five fixed encodings.
guides.found: Full-letter and consonant-only versions first met the tested reliability rule at 36 supplied training names. The internal-vowel-omission version failed its confirmation gate, and the syllable-like schemes did not reach development qualification.
guides.unresolved: Correct name pairs and boundaries were supplied. The number 36 is a benchmark-specific result, not a universal minimum or permission to fit uncertain Voynich labels.

guides.title: Does removing vowels make name recovery easier?
guides.tested: Tested several letter and syllable-like encodings on a small set of known botanical name labels with correct pairings supplied.
guides.found: None met the required reliability across the tested splits, although some recovered many transformed strings. Wrong-pair controls and unresolved units were preserved.
guides.unresolved: Recovering a consonant skeleton is not recovering a full historical name. This deliberately easy synthetic task did not qualify a Voynich sound mapping.

guides.title: What else appears beside qol and cheol?
guides.tested: Inventoried neighboring words, shared two-sided frames, and direction differences in related written forms, using controlled manuscript strata.
guides.found: The browser exposes frequent and sparse examples, cross-page recurrence, and cases outside the originally noticed adjacency. It assigns no new ingredient, operation, or timing categories.
guides.unresolved: Shared neighbors and spelling relations are descriptive. They need chance controls and independent semantic support before they can identify a function or meaning.

guides.title: Rechecking oal and possible word-boundary seams
guides.tested: Independently counted oal-containing forms and possible al/ch splits across available readings, keeping literal word boundaries explicit.
guides.found: oal occurs well beyond astronomy, including standalone examples elsewhere. Some al/ch components also appear as separate words, but exact controlled comparisons remained sparse and alternate splits were disputed.
guides.unresolved: A reusable substring is not automatically a root or morpheme. The audit did not establish the proposed seam, a function, a sound, or a star identification.

guides.title: Is oal specific to astronomy?
guides.tested: Checked claims about oal distribution and literal al/ch subdivisions against the complete available reading inventory.
guides.found: The proposed astronomy-exclusive prediction failed: oal occurs in several other sections. The broader alch count referred to substring-bearing tokens rather than standalone words, and simple proportional distribution was not established either.
guides.unresolved: A narrower rare oalch lead remains exploratory. Hand, format, coverage, and alternative word boundaries prevent a semantic interpretation.

guides.title: Checking a proposed star-and-herb correspondence chain
guides.tested: Audited the manuscript spellings and historical correspondences used to connect an oalch lead with astronomical and herbal traditions.
guides.found: Some written forms and historical associations could be sourced, but their manuscript locations did not establish a common referent. A connector label, a figure label, and paragraph text could not simply be treated as the same named star.
guides.unresolved: The botanical identification and the link from historical tradition to Voynich words remained unsupported. No sounds, prefixes, star identities, or plant identities were assigned.

guides.title: Does removing the opening erase unusual spelling?
guides.tested: Applied several predeclared initial-removal rules uniformly to candidates and comparison words, then recomputed descriptive spelling ranks.
guides.found: The opening was not the only source of atypicality: some shorter forms remained unusual. Their ranks changed with segmentation, transcription, reference set, and sometimes very small peer groups.
guides.unresolved: An unusual remainder is not a proven linguistic root or content word. Sparse astronomical reference material and unseen signs limited the comparison.

guides.title: Keeping competing subdivisions of oalcheg
guides.tested: Searched consistently for the whole word and several possible remainders after removing short openings.
guides.found: The apparent uniqueness of the full spelling did not carry over to every possible remainder; related strings occurred at additional physical locations. Competing cuts were retained rather than choosing a preferred root.
guides.unresolved: Shared endings do not prove common meaning or a functional prefix. The earlier negative cycle comparison did not establish what those openings do.

guides.title: Tracing an unusual label and its near matches
guides.tested: Searched all available readings and sections for exact and near spellings, then inspected the relevant manuscript images.
guides.found: The exact label had one physical location. Its closest botanical neighbor had disputed reading and segmentation, and a wider astronomical lead labelled a curved connector rather than an identified individual star.
guides.unresolved: Multiple transcriptions do not multiply the number of physical attestations. No admissible historical name or sound mapping was established.

guides.title: Does the opening-order pattern survive one intervening word?
guides.tested: Extended the sh/qok order comparison to three-word spans, with one readable word between the endpoints and no crossing of gaps or lines.
guides.found: The new counters passed their constructed checks, but the broad corrected manuscript search did not establish the gap effect. The earlier adjacent-order result was preserved separately.
guides.unresolved: Even a surviving gap pattern could arise from chained local transitions. Its failure would not prove a word-boundary mechanism or rule out grammar.

guides.title: Repairing the broad opening-search correction
guides.tested: Qualified a separately frozen correction based on the strongest standardized count contrast in each shuffled dataset.
guides.found: The numerical correction controls passed. This addressed the earlier test's finite-tail precision problem without relabelling its old p-values or discarding unsuccessful candidates.
guides.unresolved: This qualified a specified statistical instrument, not a language interpretation. Its scope and correction family still govern any manuscript application.

guides.title: Does sh precede qok across manuscript contexts?
guides.tested: Counted immediate written-word order separately by hand, section, variety, and reading, then compared with within-line shuffles and a broad opening-family search.
guides.found: Some raw contrasts, especially in the bath section, were strong. The original broad correction was constrained by finite-shuffle precision and did not support treating its nonpassing result as absence of order.
guides.unresolved: This version exposed a measurement limit. The relation's meaning and mechanism were unresolved, and the two transcriptions were not independent manuscript samples.

guides.title: Do opening words become ordinary words when their first sign is removed?
guides.tested: Compared initial and final sign removal at source-marked paragraph openings with matched ordinary positions and separately learned vocabularies.
guides.found: No comparison passed both readings. Some spelling matches existed, but several tests had too few pages to attain the required corrected significance level at all.
guides.unresolved: That attainable-limit problem prevents a decisive negative conclusion. Written-form membership also cannot by itself identify an opening sign's function.

guides.title: Building a fair evaluator for proposed keys and ordered names
guides.tested: Developed and revised an evaluator, trap controls, historical-source intake, name-list packets, and rules for prospective versus retrospective testing.
guides.found: The first prototype failed required scientific qualification despite passing engineering checks. The later v7.2 harness qualified on its declared scope, but the screened published keys stopped at intake without scoring. Source collations and admission amendments remain separate records.
guides.unresolved: Initial reports are historical checkpoints, not a summary of every later attempt. A qualified failure can reject a specified implementation on its tested scope, not every possible version of a broad decipherment idea.

guides.title: Why was the phrase detector missing known phrases?
guides.tested: Diagnosed sample-size, layout, and correction choices on known prose, then froze a smaller phrase-selection procedure before separate samples.
guides.found: The narrower procedure recovered several ordinary phrases and flagged none of twenty shams, meeting its limited gate. Other chosen phrases and an apostrophe artifact still failed and were retained.
guides.unresolved: This was a narrow later-herbal check with artificial lines. It did not establish medieval transfer, broad semantic qualification, or a new manuscript result.

guides.title: Can the same test detect phrases in readable text?
guides.tested: Applied the unchanged broad phrase test to known astrolabe and herbal prose placed into manuscript-like line templates.
guides.found: Some Chaucer phrases were detected, while the herbal sample did not pass in both layouts. Detection also depended on the artificial line arrangement.
guides.unresolved: Single samples are not a reliable power estimate. A negative manuscript result cannot distinguish ordinary herbal prose from other possibilities when this known herbal control also goes undetected.

guides.title: Why do phrase counts differ between transcriptions?
guides.tested: Audited the exact source locations behind the selected phrase pairs without refitting or conducting new significance tests.
guides.found: Several discrepancies came from joined versus split words or small spelling differences. The audit retained every alternate reading instead of harmonizing away the disagreement.
guides.unresolved: Parsed-text differences are not expert handwriting adjudication. The inspection did not validate the proposed semantic worksheet categories.

guides.title: Do phrases selected on some folios recur on others?
guides.tested: Selected candidate pairs on training folios, froze them, and tested separate folios with a correction across the fixed family.
guides.found: One pair passed globally in one reading but was not selected by the other. No pair achieved the required global paired success across both readings.
guides.unresolved: This used one retrospective split of already available text. Neither failure nor a one-reading success establishes a phrase's meaning or the absence of linguistic structure.

guides.title: Building a source-linked plant-name starting table
guides.tested: Collected competing plant identifications, historical written names, and the corresponding paragraph-opening slots on six illustrated folios.
guides.found: The inventory exposed blocked leads, uncertain name equivalences, and mismatches between a proposed plant and the chosen text slot. None of the plant identities was treated as confirmed.
guides.unresolved: A plausible drawing, a historical plant name, and a nearby word are three separate links that still need evidence. No sound mapping was fitted.

guides.title: Inspecting plant details and dated name forms
guides.tested: Looked at full scans and close details for the castor and pansy candidates, then checked headings in a dated historical herbal.
guides.found: The candidates remained plausible but provisional; key diagnostic features were not demonstrated and visible mismatches remained. The dated headings supplied conditional written names from one later source tradition.
guides.unresolved: The names do not establish earlier local usage, species identification, or the meaning of the paragraph opener. No sound values were fitted.

guides.title: Checking the evidence behind plant identifications
guides.tested: Revisited six plant images and the provenance of proposed botanical and historical-name matches.
guides.found: Some visual candidates remained useful, but no species was confirmed. Several apparently convenient historical name anchors were less secure than spelling resemblance suggested, and alternate identifications were retained.
guides.unresolved: Overview images and edited notebook transcriptions do not settle fine botanical details or autograph readings. The plant-to-name-to-word chain remained unqualified.

guides.title: Preparing the next controlled tests
guides.tested: Prioritized published-key intake, image/text pre-join rules, and B/C adapter primitives while parking the role-weighting variants.
guides.found: Engineering checks passed, but all three screened published keys stopped at intake without scientific scoring. Missing ratings and provenance still blocked the image/text join at this checkpoint.
guides.unresolved: Engineering parity did not replace real-support qualification. Later completion work is preserved in a separate continuation folder rather than retroactively changing this report.

guides.title: Does a noticed qo-word arrangement survive search correction?
guides.tested: Compared the selected ordering of related qo-prefixed and unprefixed word pairs with two frequency- and position-aware shuffle comparisons.
guides.found: The pattern exceeded the average shuffle, especially in one reading, but did not pass the declared search correction in either reading.
guides.unresolved: This retrospective result neither identifies a prefix's function nor demonstrates that the text lacks structure. The wider search that produced the pattern matters.

guides.title: Could the opening-removal test detect an effect if present?
guides.tested: Planted known prefix effects on layouts matching the earlier deletion experiment and checked false alarms and detection rates.
guides.found: False alarms were low in the specified controls, but detection missed the required sensitivity targets, including for strong effects. The manuscript was not rescored.
guides.unresolved: The earlier lack of a passing deletion result is therefore not a decisive absence finding. These constructed lexicons do not cover every possible language mechanism.

guides.title: Designing a test beyond adjacent transitions
guides.tested: Specified a new conditional test for one-word-gap order while fixing each span's immediate transition counts and the full original search family.
guides.found: The design was frozen as a new candidate. It aimed to address discreteness and asymmetry in the earlier test rather than select a smaller winning search.
guides.unresolved: Full qualification and manuscript scoring were not completed in this folder. A new statistic does not come with a promised sensitivity improvement.

guides.title: Which section differences survive basic matching?
guides.tested: Compared written word parts while holding writer, manuscript variety, text format, and broad word position fixed wherever support allowed.
guides.found: Several related contrasts survived in both readings, including more qo beginnings in bath text and certain ke/eol patterns in Recipes. These are overlapping families of observations rather than independent discoveries.
guides.unresolved: Some sections could not be compared fairly because coverage did not overlap. Surviving distribution differences do not identify meanings, syllables, or grammatical categories.

guides.title: Testing a proposed support rule right at its boundary
guides.tested: Constructed new layouts just above the proposed outcome-relevant support threshold, including one- and two-available-follower arrangements.
guides.found: The specified false-alarm and planted-effect checks passed in this narrow boundary suite. Fully blocked comparisons were prevented from inflating the support count.
guides.unresolved: This qualifies the rule only for the constructed arrangements tested. It is not a manuscript result or a universal guarantee at that threshold.

guides.title: Would considering every interior position solve sparse matching?
guides.tested: Allowed all interior positions as candidate matches while preserving line composition, exact word bodies, and position controls.
guides.found: The constructed positive cases still failed the required detection gates, and no dataset reached the earlier usable-support requirement. Some zero false-alarm counts came from cases that could not be estimated at all.
guides.unresolved: The limitation was too few usable comparisons, not evidence against an association. No manuscript data were opened or scored.

guides.title: Preserving whether a following word is structurally possible
guides.tested: Changed the conditional comparison so prefixes could exchange only within the same follower-availability pattern.
guides.found: This removed the earlier availability-driven alarms in the specified controls. Detection of the planted positive effects remained too weak, so broad qualification still failed.
guides.unresolved: Fixing a confound can reduce useful support. Both correct false-alarm behavior and adequate sensitivity were still needed before manuscript use.

guides.title: Counting support that can actually affect the outcome
guides.tested: Defined a support measure that gives no credit to fully blocked followers, then tested it on new constructed layouts.
guides.found: The declared controls and planted fifteen-point differences passed under the supported architectures. Separate checks showed that adding blocked cases could not artificially improve the support measure.
guides.unresolved: The pass is limited to this simulation scope and effect size. It does not establish support or an effect in every manuscript context.

guides.title: When availability creates misleading apparent effects
guides.tested: Stress-tested layouts with sharply different follower availability after ch and sh, including a joint boundary case.
guides.found: The earlier reference comparison produced many nuisance-only alarms because it failed to preserve the prefix/availability relationship. The apparent outcome association could arise through availability alone.
guides.unresolved: These were failures for a claim beyond availability, not examples of a truly association-free dataset being flagged. The finding motivated a better conditional comparison.

guides.title: Mapping the association across contexts
guides.tested: Compared sh/ch-to-qok effects across manuscript contexts using separate readings and explicit support and control checks.
guides.found: Some retrospective panels passed, including starred text in both readings; other apparently positive effects were blocked by failed null qualification. The descriptive map retained all these differences.
guides.unresolved: A large-looking effect cannot rescue a failed comparison instrument. Context variation does not identify grammar, meaning, or a scribe-independent mechanism.

guides.title: Can a predictor separate local writing from longer context?
guides.tested: Compared bounded local predictors with extended-context alternatives on constructed mechanisms before fitting manuscript data.
guides.found: The first attempt failed its required adequacy or power gate and did not proceed to manuscript fitting. An explicit equal-output control showed that a grammar-like rule and a phrase template could look identical to the test.
guides.unresolved: Even an extended-context gain would only reject the specified limited comparator. It could not uniquely establish grammar.

guides.title: A revised context predictor with limited qualification
guides.tested: Introduced training-only hierarchical backoff while keeping the main feature, support, and qualification rules fixed.
guides.found: The revision passed a limited control scope, but none of the twenty-four corrected manuscript comparisons passed. Small descriptive junction gains did not settle the mechanism.
guides.unresolved: The retained observational-equivalence control still prevents a unique grammar-versus-template conclusion. Negative comparisons do not eliminate every contextual model.

guides.title: Separating diluted effects from too few comparable words
guides.tested: Used paired constructed layouts to distinguish effect dilution from the loss of matching support when more exact word bodies are introduced.
guides.found: The experiment showed why a nominally planted effect could become smaller at eligible followers and why more diverse bodies could leave very few comparable cases. Correcting the target effect did not automatically restore power.
guides.unresolved: These are controlled engineering explanations of a failed instrument, not observations about the manuscript's mechanism. Infeasible constructions were retained rather than forced into the test.

guides.title: Does the association depend on ending families?
guides.tested: Made a frozen descriptive breakdown by the original ending families while auditing which family outcomes had already been examined.
guides.found: The report distinguished discovery contexts, the known origin of the idea, and additional descriptive contexts. It required each individual family to have support rather than rescuing sparse families by pooling.
guides.unresolved: These are exposed, retrospective counts with no inferential p-values. The grouped descriptions cannot be promoted to fresh confirmation or an ending's meaning.

guides.title: Comparing sh and ch with endings and bodies matched
guides.tested: Tested whether the next-word qok difference survives same-page ending-family controls and a stronger exact-body comparison.
guides.found: The bath association reproduced in both main readings under the ending comparison. The starred comparisons did not clear the declared correction, and exact-body bath results were mixed across readings.
guides.unresolved: The stronger two-scribe grammar claim did not qualify. Spelling, junction effects, and collocations remained possible explanations, and some borderline results had simulation uncertainty.

guides.title: Expanding the set of legal comparison arrangements
guides.tested: Built an exact conditional comparison over more prefix arrangements while retaining line, position, and literal-body controls.
guides.found: The revision improved detection in some constructed cases, but a required page-control gate and sparse positive cases still failed. Every result from the new and old methods on the same data was retained.
guides.unresolved: A larger legal arrangement space is not automatically a fully qualified test. Sparse support and nuisance behavior still constrained manuscript use.

guides.title: Looking at the ey ending by itself
guides.tested: Made a retrospective breakdown of next-qok rates for the original ey ending family across the recorded contexts, keeping eey separate.
guides.found: The saved counts show substantial context differences and retain the separate sh/ch arms and availability-restricted views. This was a description after earlier family results had been seen.
guides.unresolved: No significance tests or confidence intervals were calculated. The counts do not establish an ey meaning, a universal suppression rule, or independent confirmation.

guides.title: Comparing ey with other ending families
guides.tested: Compared observed next-qok rates after ey with pooled edy/y/other endings, excluding eey on both sides.
guides.found: The direction varied by context: ey had a higher raw rate in bath text and lower rates in some other material. The table distinguishes this ending comparison from the earlier sh-minus-ch effect.
guides.unresolved: The pooled comparison does not adjust for page or opener composition. It is a post-hoc description, not a causal or inferential result.

guides.title: Matching the ey comparison within page and opener
guides.tested: Refined the ending comparison by using only page-and-opener groups containing both ending categories.
guides.found: The matched tables show how much of each raw contrast remains after the recorded page and sh/ch composition are held fixed. Sparse groups and separate reading/view results remain visible.
guides.unresolved: The refinement was chosen after the raw contrasts were known. It supplies descriptive adjustment rather than a new independent test or causal estimate.

guides.title: Does one folio drive the ey comparison?
guides.tested: Repeated the matched descriptive comparison while omitting one whole recorded folio at a time in botanical and Rosettes contexts.
guides.found: Some botanical comparisons could change sign under a single omission, while the listed Rosettes omissions retained the lower-ey direction. Zero-weight omissions were retained explicitly.
guides.unresolved: Stability under these omissions is not independent replication or statistical significance. Small and dependent source populations still limit interpretation.

guides.title: Inspecting an influential folio's actual counts
guides.tested: Examined the ey-versus-other-ending counts on f31r after the omission analysis identified its influence.
guides.found: The strong-looking local gap depended on very small ey counts, including zero following qok events in the two sh/ey examples. Restricting to available followers reduced the comparison denominator while retaining its qok events.
guides.unresolved: The page was selected after its influence was known. These transparent counts are not a fresh test or evidence of a general ey rule.

guides.title: Testing the point where a planted effect is just possible
guides.tested: Constructed supported layouts near the sh follower-availability boundary, retaining accepted and rejected candidate layouts.
guides.found: The specified null and positive checks passed at that particular boundary. The positive was deliberately strong among the few available followers, which can make it easier to detect.
guides.unresolved: The ch boundary and the joint boundary were not qualified by this experiment. A pass here is not universal sensitivity across availability patterns.

guides.title: Constructing enough exact-body comparisons without rejection sampling
guides.tested: Built new layouts with four literal word bodies and balanced page support just above the proposed support boundary.
guides.found: The constructed suite passed the declared false-alarm and planted-positive gates. Layouts were fixed before outcomes, and every one was retained.
guides.unresolved: This is limited synthetic qualification for the specified construction. It does not establish that the manuscript supplies comparable support.

guides.title: Preparing an independently labelled image-context test
guides.tested: Separated line registration and picture judgments from the already exposed text events, with withheld ambiguous panels and controlled handoff packets.
guides.found: The retained checkpoint is pending workflow, not a manuscript finding. A fresh-session eligibility probe encountered inherited project context and stopped before opening the permitted inputs.
guides.unresolved: A fresh chat or process alone does not prove the required blinding. Registration, independent ratings, agreement, support, and qualification were still needed before the outcome join.

guides.title: Combining support and effect-feasibility requirements
guides.tested: Tested a proposed gate requiring usable prefix rearrangements, page coverage, and enough available followers to support the planted effect.
guides.found: The one-body construction passed its cells, but the four-body branch could not supply the frozen quota within its attempt cap. The joint qualification therefore failed.
guides.unresolved: An incomplete qualification is different from low power or a negative manuscript result. The cap was not extended after outcomes were seen.

guides.title: Controlling both line composition and exact position
guides.tested: Permitted matched prefix swaps that preserve page, line composition, exact positions, and literal word bodies.
guides.found: The specified nuisance controls passed, but smaller and sparse planted effects failed broad sensitivity requirements. Conditioning on more information removed much of the usable variation.
guides.unresolved: Correct nuisance handling does not ensure useful power. No manuscript result was produced or rescored here.

guides.title: Planting the effect in the comparisons the test actually uses
guides.tested: Adjusted constructed qok probabilities so that the movable matched comparisons had the intended effect, keeping structural zeros explicit.
guides.found: The analytic target effect could be made correct where feasible, but many layouts still had too little matching support to detect it. Unsupported and infeasible cases stayed in the record.
guides.unresolved: A correctly planted effect does not guarantee a powerful test. These synthetic layouts did not establish manuscript eligibility or a writing mechanism.

guides.title: Could non-grammatical mechanisms produce the association?
guides.tested: Reused the existing manuscript audit and tested new constructed page, position, junction, and other local mechanisms against its comparison rules.
guides.found: The bath association remained a recorded structural finding, but the stress tests showed why controlling some nuisances does not uniquely identify its cause. Stronger exact-body evidence was mixed across readings.
guides.unresolved: Grammar, contextual spelling, junction effects, and collocations were not separated conclusively. No new manuscript fit was used to rescue the claim.

guides.title: Does the manuscript supply enough legal exact matches?
guides.tested: Audited eligible lines and readable following slots under the frozen exact matching rule without calculating qok outcomes.
guides.found: All four target panels had zero informative matching support under this rule. Many readable words therefore did not translate into usable controlled comparisons.
guides.unresolved: Unsupported is not a negative association result. No outcome classification, effect score, or p-value was calculated.

guides.title: Is exact-position matching enough to remove nuisance effects?
guides.tested: Qualified a conditional comparison matching page, line length, exact position, and word body on constructed cases.
guides.found: Position control helped, but a shared line-level setting still produced misleading signals and a required page-control bound also failed. The method remained unqualified.
guides.unresolved: The experiment identified an omitted line-level nuisance, rather than a manuscript mechanism. No real text was rescored.

guides.title: Distinguishing limited certification precision from a demonstrated bias
guides.tested: Diagnosed the small earlier control banks, then retained a separately frozen, much larger follow-up and a permutation-bank diagnosis of the old heterogeneity test.
guides.found: The completed follow-up qualified the declared A/Q1 cells under its constructed scope. The original near-miss statuses remained preserved, and extra inner shuffles did not automatically resolve the separate B-Q2 problem.
guides.unresolved: The root diagnostic report precedes the completed run. More precise control certification does not make exposed manuscript material fresh or automatically promote previously blocked results.

guides.title: Relaxing exact position to recover comparisons
guides.tested: Grouped same-body pairs by relative line position while preserving retained-line composition and follower availability.
guides.found: The original-volume constructed cases were unsupported. A larger-volume sensitivity improved support in some regimes, but the full candidate remained unqualified.
guides.unresolved: Four times as many active lines is a different sample-size experiment, not evidence that the original material was adequate. Relaxed matching still needed nuisance checks.

guides.title: Applying the completed control qualification transparently
guides.tested: Reassessed the specified, already exposed manuscript comparisons using the completed control follow-up while leaving the original files unchanged.
guides.found: The specified association comparisons passed their retained search corrections in both readings. The separate test of differences between contexts remained unqualified and still counted toward its original correction family.
guides.unresolved: These are retrospective results, not new material or independent replication. The corrections do not account for every search made throughout the project's history.

guides.title: A targeted retrospective association retest
guides.tested: Froze a next-qok question, support rules, control checks, and separate predictive comparisons for previously searched non-bathing material.
guides.found: The primary P1 association passed in both readings; P2 lacked the required support or qualification. The extra context-prediction and transported interaction checks did not supply a passing mechanism result.
guides.unresolved: The combined panels were not untouched, and the readings were not independent replications. The adjacency result does not establish grammar or explain its cause.

guides.title: Catching an incompatible specification before running it
guides.tested: Checked whether the requested single-target study could be executed unchanged by the referenced scoring engines.
guides.found: Preflight found a mismatch between the requested strata and the qualified engine, plus target leakage in a proposed predictive comparison. All manuscript cells stayed not run.
guides.unresolved: Not run is different from unsupported, underpowered, or negative. Executing the study required an explicit revised specification rather than silently changing its question.

guides.title: How sample size and matching layout affect sensitivity
guides.tested: Varied the number of lines, fragmentation of exact word bodies, and the way legal position pairs were selected on new constructed data.
guides.found: The full factorial records show where legal rearrangements and attainable significance disappear, and where body-informed selection helps. A nonconstant test can still have no outcome capable of passing its correction.
guides.unresolved: These diagnostics do not establish adequate manuscript power or enumerate every legal arrangement. No manuscript data were scored.

guides.title: Developing an interaction test for sparse parts
guides.tested: Prepared covariates, matching profiles, identifiability checks, and a frozen constructed-data qualification schedule for the sparse-context interaction study.
guides.found: This snapshot contains per-trial records and qualification progress, including a recorded interruption and resume. It does not contain a completed owning results report that establishes an overall scientific pass.
guides.unresolved: Progress records and passing individual cells are not a completed qualification. No manuscript conclusion should be inferred from the existence of the runner or its saved trials.

guides.title: Which realistic changes destroy usable support?
guides.tested: Varied line length, origin position, target-word replacement, and unknown slots separately and together, using support-only constructed data.
guides.found: Even modest changes could push layouts below the unchanged support requirement. Combining length shifts and sparse identities reduced support much more than the idealized baseline suggested.
guides.unresolved: This generated no qok outcomes and tested no manuscript association. It explains a pipeline bottleneck rather than demonstrating a writing mechanism.

guides.title: Checking sensitivity just above the proposed support cutoff
guides.tested: Tested new aligned and fragmented constructed layouts close to the minimum usable-support boundary, with page-concentration limits.
guides.found: The declared nuisance and planted-positive gates passed for the specified arrangements and effect sizes. Rejected layouts and all attempted seeds remained in the record.
guides.unresolved: This limited boundary qualification is not a universal guarantee, an independently chosen minimum, or evidence that real manuscript panels meet the rule.

guides.title: Defining a minimum amount of usable comparison
guides.tested: Proposed a support rule based on legal prefix reassignment, page coverage, and concentration, without selecting on qok outcomes.
guides.found: The admitted constructed cases met the limited declared qualification, while many sparse layouts were excluded. The rule measures usable comparisons rather than the total number of readable words.
guides.unresolved: It was not proved to be the smallest sufficient threshold or sensitive to arbitrarily small effects. Manuscript support still had to be checked separately.

guides.title: Testing the full path from raw tokens to a score
guides.tested: Exercised token cleaning, eligibility, body matching, availability conditioning, support, and exact scoring together on constructed transcription.
guides.found: Dense designed cases passed, but sparse cases lost eligibility and were unsupported. The complete pipeline therefore did not receive broad qualification.
guides.unresolved: Good performance on idealized group layouts cannot establish performance after realistic token and position losses. No manuscript scoring ran.

guides.title: A focused distant-context interaction score
guides.tested: Replaced a broad prediction search with one interaction score learned on separate folios and tested under several constructed nuisance and signal regimes.
guides.found: The first focused score failed its frozen qualification. All inadequate and unsupported positives were counted as nondetections, and failed development examples were retained.
guides.unresolved: Even a successful interaction score could not uniquely distinguish grammar from a phrase template, latent register, or contextual spelling. No meaning was assigned.

guides.title: Repairing the nuisance predictor without moving the gates
guides.tested: Changed only the nuisance-estimation procedure while retaining the split, interaction target, adequacy rule, and required control thresholds.
guides.found: The repair passed a limited synthetic scope, but none of the four manuscript panels qualified. Some panels were uninformative because no direction was learned, rather than demonstrating a negative effect.
guides.unresolved: A constructed-data pass and a stored p-value of one are not themselves manuscript findings. The mechanism and broader transfer remained unresolved.

guides.title: Is the shedy–middle–shedy frame unusually recurrent?
guides.tested: Tested both the frame's total count and the recurrence of distinct middle words under two position/frequency-aware null comparisons.
guides.found: One H-only middle-recurrence comparison passed one corrected screen. Total frequency did not pass, and the result did not become a consistent paired finding across readings and controls.
guides.unresolved: The conclusion depends on the chosen comparison model. No middle word was assigned an operation, attribute, timing, or medicinal meaning.

guides.title: Why did a simple substitution search fail on known text?
guides.tested: Compared repeated searches, sample size, and word ordering using fresh positions in the same known source works.
guides.found: More search starts repaired the old control failures, and the larger samples recovered the constructed mappings. Remaining small-sample failures exposed unseen letters and, in one case, an objective favoring a wrong key.
guides.unresolved: This did not establish independent-work transfer, semantic reading, or manuscript decoding. Better search performance should not be mistaken for a recovered language.

guides.title: Can the proposed search recover even a known letter substitution?
guides.tested: Froze unusual-word candidates but first tested the restricted search on short known-text substitution problems in Latin, Middle English, and German.
guides.found: Each language failed at least one required control, so all three language gates failed and no manuscript key was fitted.
guides.unresolved: This is a limitation of that search and sample size, not a rejection of phonetic or rebus writing. A list of unusual forms supplies no sound values by itself.

guides.title: Trying a restricted whole-written-syllable mapping
guides.tested: Required each cipher group to stand for a complete candidate written syllable and tested known-answer controls before manuscript application.
guides.found: None of the three fresh controls qualified. Missing inventory coverage and poor recovery persisted even with true group boundaries supplied.
guides.unresolved: Only one restricted Latin method and syllable definition were tested. The failure does not reject syllabic writing, and no manuscript scores were produced.

guides.title: Preparing a diagnosis of the syllable decoder
guides.tested: Specified objective, search, coverage, and sample-size checks for the failed syllable method, with frozen fresh-control mappings.
guides.found: The retained folder contains the protocol, source-coverage information, inventories, keys, and diagnostic setup. It does not contain a completed result report or a verified successful follow-up.
guides.unresolved: The preceding failure remains intact. Proposed refinements and prepared keys are not evidence that syllable recovery was repaired or that manuscript scoring opened.

guides.title: Preparing source and generator comparisons for writing-system hypotheses
guides.tested: Built known-source corpora, constructed writing-system controls, coverage checks, and staged hypothesis definitions before fresh-reserve testing.
guides.found: The later development source cut resolved its recorded size and literal-unit coverage gaps, and arithmetic/engineering checks passed within their scope. The claim definitions and H3 remained unresolved.
guides.unresolved: Development qualification did not open fresh reserves or establish full recovery, model survival, or a manuscript fit. Register, source, and glyph-coverage differences remained explicit.

guides.title: Do completed picture labels support a text comparison?
guides.tested: Froze exact rater agreement as the label rule, audited readable support without joining real word outcomes, and ran controls on the actual geometry.
guides.found: All lines had two ratings, but disagreements remained unresolved rather than missing. The primary comparison had no eligible folios, and the scan failed required calibration and sensitivity checks.
guides.unresolved: Good overall annotation agreement does not create within-context comparison support. The real word/image outcome join and protected scoring remained closed.

guides.title: Why did the picture-label scan produce too many alarms?
guides.tested: Traced the failed scan through its exact readable exposures, permutation assumptions, sparse cells, and a separately frozen repair diagnostic.
guides.found: The audit identified a mismatch between fixed label-specific readable exposure and the shuffled reference, with a particularly influential singleton cell. Position confounding and support failures were separate problems. The saved repair cell reduced alarms but still failed its scan gate.
guides.unresolved: The retained repair summary is limited and does not certify a complete replacement. No real word/image outcome join or protected scoring followed from the audit.

guides.title: Does qokedy precede ol and qol more than the controls predict?
guides.tested: Tested the proposed directional ordering with a primary exact-position method and a separately retained within-line sensitivity.
guides.found: The primary method failed its planted-effect power gate and was not run on the manuscript. The permitted sensitivity supplied only a limited F-reading result, without the primary comparison.
guides.unresolved: A one-reading sensitivity cannot replace the failed primary test or identify syntax. Low control sensitivity is not evidence that manuscript ordering is absent.

guides.title: Are some word positions unusually spelled for a simple template?
guides.tested: Learned written-character pair models on separate folios and compared word-position surprise while matching length and training frequency.
guides.found: The hand-2 botanical first/interior comparison passed in both readings, with the same direction on all seven test folios. Other comparisons failed or lacked support.
guides.unresolved: The training sample was small and the split retrospective. Model-relative unusualness is not proof of a name, pronunciation, or phonetic encoding.

guides.title: Does one-word-gap order exceed immediate-transition structure?
guides.tested: Held each readable span's endpoints, word inventory, and immediate sh/qok/other transition counts fixed while testing the longer-gap contrast.
guides.found: No gap result passed the retained broad correction. The exact null had real variation and adequate numerical resolution, so the old rank-floor explanation did not apply here.
guides.unresolved: The test fixes the adjacent association by design and cannot erase or retest it. Failure to detect a residual does not prove that immediate transitions fully explain the text.

guides.title: Where was the longer-gap test losing sensitivity?
guides.tested: Held the planted alternative fixed while varying the search correction, separating the cost of conditioning from the cost of a broad search.
guides.found: The diagnostic quantified how the full search family and error budget reduced detection. Easier counterfactual screens could detect more, but were not substituted for the frozen acceptance rule.
guides.unresolved: The earlier qualification remained failed. No robustness bank was resumed and no manuscript was rescored.

guides.title: Qualifying a broad correction under fixed local transitions
guides.tested: Tested exact sampling, numerical resolution, false alarms, and planted effects while preserving the full original search family and local-transition constraints.
